question: A 17-year-old high school student is brought to the emergency department because of irritability and rapid breathing. He appears agitated and is diaphoretic. His temperature is 38.3°C (101°F), pulse is 129/min, respirations are 28/min, and blood pressure is 158/95 mmHg. His pupils are dilated. An ECG shows sinus tachycardia. Which of the following substances is used to make the drug this patient has most likely taken?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Pseudoephedrine -> sympathomimetic effects -> increased heart rate and blood pressure -> 90%
analysis: The patient is presenting with symptoms suggestive of sympathomimetic toxicity, likely due to an amphetamine-like substance. The combination of irritability, rapid breathing, agitation, diaphoresis, dilated pupils, tachycardia, and hypertension is concerning for amphetamine use.
